MARKET.head: ProWine Mumbai to showcase India's wine and spirits market to global producers in November
MARKET.summ: India’s growing appeal to international wine and spirits producers will take center stage at ProWine Mumbai this month, as rising disposable incomes, demand for premium drinks and new trade agreements open opportunities in the market
takeaways: ProWine Mumbai runs November 18-19 at Jio World Convention Centre, expecting over 200 exhibitors and 6,000 trade visitors.
India has free trade agreements with Australia, the UK and New Zealand, and concluded EU negotiations in January 2026, cutting some import tariffs.
The event is organized by Messe Düsseldorf India and All Things Nice, with 12 national pavilions and over 1,000 brands.

MARKET.head: Australian white wine exports to China more than double in volume in Q3
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian wine exports to mainland China rose 1.9% by value in Q3 2026 while global exports fell 7.3%.
White wine export volumes to mainland China rose 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data.
Mainland China accounted for about 59% of Australia's global export value for wines priced at A$10 per liter or more.

MARKET.head: Two Hampshire winemakers launch joint celebration wine collective with Winchester tasting
MARKET.summ: Chalkdown English Sparkling Wine and The B58 Winery, two of Hampshire’s independent winemakers, are launching the Hampshire Celebration Collective, a new partnership created to bring local wines to the county’s
takeaways: Chalkdown English Sparkling Wine and The B58 Winery launch the Hampshire Celebration Collective, a partnership selling local wines for occasions.
A free tasting runs Thursday 19 November, 5pm to 7pm, at Kingsgate Wines & Provisions in Winchester, with an on-the-night discount.
The Collective offers bespoke pricing, mix-and-match cases with a one-case minimum, and all wines are made in the producers' own Hampshire wineries.

MARKET.head: Shanghai wine trader WINEXSH files for bankruptcy liquidation amid falling prices
MARKET.summ: Shanghai-based fine wine trader WINEXSH has applied for bankruptcy liquidation, with a supplier reporting an unpaid order and Chinese wine media citing complaints from customers unable to collect wines or secure refunds
takeaways: Shanghai Free Trade Zone Wine Exchange, known as WINEXSH, has applied for liquidation at Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court.
The court reportedly held a hearing on October 29, but records do not show whether the application has been accepted.
A former Bordeaux supplier says WINEXSH left an en primeur order unpaid, with the wines uncollected, as fine wine prices in China fell.

MARKET.head: Western Australian wineries sell well at two-day Shanghai festival
MARKET.summ: A two-day Discover Western Australian Festival drew nearly 900 people in Shanghai, with exhibitors reporting stronger-than-expected consumer sales and new business prospects among distributors, restaurants and hotels
takeaways: Discover Western Australia Festival in Shanghai drew nearly 600 consumers on November 7 and about 300 trade professionals on November 8.
Exhibitors from 17 Margaret River and Great Southern wineries reported sales beyond expectations, with some flagship wines sold via Red Note.
Importers cited unmet demand, with Willoughby Park's distributor For U Global lacking stock to fill on-the-spot purchases.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria partner on three-year Victorian industry projects
MARKET.summ: A new partnership between Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will fund a range of projects across the Victorian wine industry supporting grapegrowers and winemakers.
takeaways: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will fund Victorian wine industry projects over three years, aligned with the Victorian Wine Strategy 2025-2030.
The program combines $540,000 in Victorian Government funding secured by Wine Victoria with $346,667 from Wine Australia's AWFF.
Projects will cover sustainability, biosecurity, data-driven decisions and export capability, delivered through workshops, webinars and digital tools.

MARKET.head: AI's energy, e-waste and water footprint threatens wine's green image
MARKET.summ: The Australian and New Zealand wine sector prides itself on sustainability. The very concept has become the industry’s bread and butter, quite frankly. Look at any winery website and you’ll find a dedicated page filled with paragraphs detailing all the initiatives reducing carbon emissions, saving water and limiting energy use...
takeaways: Australian and New Zealand wineries heavily promote sustainability, but AI-generated content is spreading across wine marketing and labels.
Training one large language model is estimated to emit roughly 300,000 kg of CO₂, equal to about 105 cars driven 15,000 km a year.
Global data centres could consume 945 TWh of electricity by 2030, with AI accounting for 40% of that demand.

MARKET.head: Wine still Australia's top-bought alcohol category as drinking moderates
MARKET.summ: New research shows that wine endures as “the most widely purchased category” in Australia at 55%, followed by spirits at 46% and beer at 44%. The new ‘What’s Driving Australia’s Alcohol Shopper: Consumption, Channels, Promotions and Occasions’ report from Vypr and Shop! ANZ found that 41% of Australians are drinking less than a...
takeaways: Vypr and Shop! ANZ report finds 55% of Australians buy wine, ahead of spirits at 46% and beer at 44%.
41% of Australians drink less than a year ago or have stopped, while only 6% drink more.
48% of shoppers now typically spend over $40 per liquor-store visit, up from about 23% a year ago.

MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and PGI wines to Chinese buyers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: Twenty-three Moldovan wine and spirits producers will seek Chinese importers and distributors at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12.
Moldovan wine imports to China reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026, per Chinese customs data.
About 85% of Moldova's wine production is exported, with the EU taking roughly 60% of wine exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine's small-format packs gain ground with moderation and single-person households
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined export and domestic off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22 per cent to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39 per cent, from 450,000 litres in 2023-24 to 620,000 litres in 2025-26.
Census data shows 26 per cent of Australian households are single-person, up from 18 per cent in 1981.

MARKET.head: VinePair weekly roundup spans beer, spirits and wine industry headlines
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Stoli’s return to the U.S., Modelo’s deal with the NCAA, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: Covered items include Stoli's return to the U.S., Modelo as NCAA official beer, and RNDC's Chapter 11 liquidation.
Other items cover U.S. household alcohol spending, EU approval of Chianti rosé, and a Diageo chemical spill.

CULTURE.head: ASVO honours AWRI's Mark Krstic and Treasury's James Godfrey for industry service
CULTURE.summ: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) celebrates the work of long-established wine career professionals. This year, AWRI’s Mark Krstic was honoured as the ASVO’s 31st ‘Fellow of the Society’ and Treasury Wine Estate’s James Godfrey was recognised through a newly created ‘Lifetime Acknowledgement Award’.
takeaways: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology named AWRI managing director Dr Mark Krstic its 2026 Fellow of the Society, its 31st.
Treasury Wine Estates winemaker James Godfrey received the newly created Lifetime Acknowledgement Award, particularly for his work with fortified wines.
Godfrey has declared his recent retirement, while Krstic's tenure as AWRI managing director is drawing to a close.

CULTURE.head: Victorian Wine Show names Point Leo Estate Chardonnay Best Wine of Show
CULTURE.summ: The trophy winners for the 46th Annual Victorian Wine Show (VWS) have been announced with a “healthy mix of emerging smaller wineries and seasoned campaigners celebrating success”. The judging took place in Nagambie over three intensive days, with a total of 612 entries from 124 wineries. The annual show “recognises excellence...
takeaways: The 46th Victorian Wine Show, judged in Nagambie over three days, received 612 entries from 124 wineries.
Point Leo Estate's 2024 Reserve Chardonnay won Best Wine of Show, and Pfeiffer Wines was named Most Successful Exhibitor.
Hirsch Hill's 2026 Garnacha Blanca, its first vintage of the variety, won Best Iberian Variety Wine.

CULTURE.head: ASVO names 2026 Viticulturist and Winemaker of the Year and science award winners
CULTURE.summ: Last night, the Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) revealed the winners of its Awards for Excellence. The ASVO said the winners were chosen from a very high calibre and diverse range of submissions showing expertise across winemaking, viticulture and wine science. Highlights of the evening included the naming...
takeaways: Chris Dent, owner of Gorton Drive Estate and chair of Murray Valley Winegrowers, was named 2026 ASVO Viticulturist of the Year.
David Bicknell of Oakridge Wines, with almost 25 years at the estate, was named 2026 ASVO Winemaker of the Year.
Tracey Siebert of the AWRI received the Wine Science and Technology Award, with around 2,800 citations across 48 indexed publications.

CULTURE.head: Marlborough viticulturist Anna Kelland wins 2026 Young Horticulturist of the Year title
CULTURE.summ: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland has won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title, having “excelled” in an intensive two-day competition in Auckland from 4-5 November. Kelland was the 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year and therefore went through to represent the viticulture sector in this year’s...
takeaways: Anna Kelland, a Marlborough viticulture technician for Constellation Brands, won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title in Auckland on 4-5 November.
She beat four rivals from grower, arborist, amenity and plant producer sectors, winning cash and prizes totalling more than $25,000.
Kelland is the tenth Young Viticulturist to take the title, after 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year status.

SCIENCE.head: Electrical conductivity mapping guides Burgundy's Cellier aux Moines vineyard soil digging
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, uses electrical conductivity mapping to read soil differences below the surface.
Owner Philippe Pascal's maps guided over 30 soil pits, revealing limestone density differences about 1.5 meters deep.
In 2026, a tressed Pinot Noir parcel reached 13.6% potential alcohol versus 14.5% for a conventionally trimmed neighbor.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vitcultural Innovation in the Wine Region of the Year
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Dave Pittard of Buttonwood Grove Winery and Six Eighty Cellars
NEWSLETTERS.author: Beyond Organic Wine
takeaways: Dave Pittard and wife Melissa own Buttonwood Grove Winery and Six Eighty Cellars, with about 72 acres of vines in the Finger Lakes, New York.
A Buttonwood Grove Riesling won the 2017 Governor's Cup, New York's best wine award.
Dave Pittard grows close to 30 grape varieties, including hybrids and vinifera, in a region named American Wine Region of the Year 2025 by Wine Enthusiast.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wineries Are Getting High on Real Life
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Why the World’s Most Quixotic Vineyard Needs You, Organic Demand Outstrips Supply in U.S., and the rest of the Good + Tasty news you need because *MONDAY*
NEWSLETTERS.author: Kathleen Willcox
takeaways: Joel Peterson's.
Randall Grahm, 73, is seeking a new owner or steward for his Popelouchum vineyard, as Parkinson's and mobility problems limit his work.
Grahm says his daughter Amélie has cooled on taking over Popelouchum since 'The Terroirist' documentary was filmed.

NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly dig through the pile of wine samples that show up on my doorstep, asking
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Say It Because the Science Says So: Wine Is Good For Your Health
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Overlooked, comprehensive study demonstrates regular, moderate red wine drinking improves our health
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tom Wark
takeaways: Jeffrey S. Wojtowicz's systematic review in Cureus covers 74 studies published between 1987 and 2023 on regular, moderate red wine intake.
Wojtowicz reports no negative health impact from regular moderate red wine consumption, with beneficial effects seen for mortality, dementia, certain cancers and cardiovascular conditions.
The author says the study received no media coverage, though it has been cited in 20 research papers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: How Much Should a Good Bottle of Wine Cost?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A closer look at what goes into the price of a bottle, and how much you really need to spend for quality
NEWSLETTERS.author: George Nordahl
takeaways: Setting a wine's price begins with production cost plus margin, and a US rule of thumb says distribution price is roughly double production cost.
The author models two hypothetical Spanish wineries: a large mechanised producer (Producer A) and an organic boutique producer (Producer B), focusing on the UK market.
Producer A's ex-cellar price is calculated at €2.27 (£1.89), versus €9.35 (£7.80) for Producer B, before UK duty, packaging and retail costs.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Friday 5 #201
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How you can do better than Majestic’s Black Friday deals, this month’s cookbook giveaway and some surprising things to do with sherry
NEWSLETTERS.author: Fiona Beckett
takeaways: Fiona Beckett's Friday 5 #201 includes nine top buys from Majestic at £10 or under on mix six.
This month's cookbook giveaway is Calum Franklin's The Modern Pie Maker.
The newsletter also includes a postscript from a Bordeaux tasting held this week.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Affordability: A fine $11 Argentine red
NEWSLETTERS.summ: It usually takes a little effort to scout out a really good wine value, but every now and then a great bargain just pops up right in front of you
NEWSLETTERS.author: Robin Garr
takeaways: Trivento 2023 Mendoza "Maximum" Red Blend, from Argentina's Mendoza region, retails for an $11 average in the U.S., per Wine-Searcher.com.
The blend is equal parts Uco Valley Cabernet Sauvignon and Luján de Cuyo Malbec, at 13.5% alcohol, imported by Eagle Peak Estates.
The reviewer calls it a remarkable value for everyday drinking with meals, expected to remain enjoyable through at least 2028.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Five Minutes with... Rick Rainey & Léana Godard of Forge Cellars
NEWSLETTERS.summ: On Cabernet Franc’s untapped potential, giving Finger Lakes terroir a seat at the table, and why it’s all about joy
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Forge Cellars, established in 2011 on Seneca Lake in New York's Finger Lakes, began its Cabernet Franc program with the 2019 vintage.
Forge now makes four single-vineyard Cabernet Francs from different soils, including Willow (sand), Railroad (gravel), Arlo (clay) and Bellows (sand and rock).
In 2023 Forge left stems out entirely to read each soil's tannin potential, then reintroduced stems in some wines in 2024.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Free Market Distribution: Nobody Has to Help You
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Four or five dozen companies decide whether your wine reaches a British drinker in any volumes, and that number is falling
NEWSLETTERS.author: Robert Joseph
takeaways: Tesco may buy Majestic Wine and Enotria & Coe, per industry gossip; Tesco already owns Booker since 2018.
C&C merged its subsidiaries Bibendum and Matthew Clark this year; Activequity acquired Liberty and brought it under the same roof as Alliance.
The author estimates four or five dozen significant national UK distributors, many focused on small numbers of countries and regions, shrinking options for wineries.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Friday Flash on Wine Vol. 21
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Where Do the Aromas in Wine Come From? - Oak Influence, Part 2
NEWSLETTERS.author: Lee Seeger
takeaways: Larger oak barrels give less oak influence, since less wine contacts the wood per unit volume, while smaller barrels give more.
Barrels become effectively neutral after being used three or four times, with first-use barrels giving the most dramatic oak influence.
Oak lactones, which add vanilla and coconut aromas, are released into wine on contact, and light toasting produces more lactones than heavy toasting.
